question: Which Gateway IPv6 bind contract should OpenClaw expose for LAN/custom BYOH deployments?
rationale: The implementation choice changes non-loopback Gateway reachability and upgrade semantics, and repository policy treats Gateway bind/config/security behavior as maintainer-owned rather than a safe automatic repair.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in dual-stack contract
options.body: Introduce a documented IPv6 or dual-stack bind mode/path with security warnings, platform listener semantics, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Change LAN/custom in place
options.body: Make existing `lan` or `customBindHost` accept IPv6 directly, accepting the compatibility and global IPv6 exposure risk as the new behavior for those modes.

options.title: Keep IPv4-only core
options.body: Leave core bind behavior IPv4-only and continue documenting reverse-proxy or sidecar workarounds for IPv6-only platforms.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in dual-stack contract
recommendation.body: Introduce a documented IPv6 or dual-stack bind mode/path with security warnings, platform listener semantics, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main history signal for the Gateway network resolver and related security-sensitive bind behavior.
